title: 2026 UK ETS maritime registry and surrender QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for maritime: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: The maritime operator holding account is a UK ETS Registry compliance account used to record emissions figures and receive, hold and surrender allowances.
facts.expected_handling: Keep registry account functions distinct from emissions measurement systems.

facts.source_fact: Only UK allowances can be held and used for compliance in the UK ETS Registry.
facts.expected_handling: Reject non-UK allowance instruments for UK ETS surrender.

facts.source_fact: One authorised representative with surrender-only permission is sufficient to surrender allowances from a maritime operator holding account.
facts.expected_handling: Apply surrender permission rules separately from transfer rules.

facts.source_fact: Transfers out to other accounts require permissions involving at least two authorised representatives under the default account settings.
facts.expected_handling: Do not apply one-person surrender permission to allowance transfers.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency creates the maritime operator holding account when it issues the emissions monitoring plan.
facts.expected_handling: Do not expect a compliance account before the monitoring plan is issued.

facts.source_fact: The surrender deadline for the 2026 and 2027 maritime scheme years is 23:59 UK time on 30 April 2028.
facts.expected_handling: Use the combined first-two-year surrender deadline.

facts.source_fact: From the 2028 scheme year onward, the surrender deadline is 23:59 UK time on 30 April in the following year.
facts.expected_handling: Apply annual following-year surrender timing from 2028 onward.

facts.source_fact: Allowances must still be surrendered by the deadline even if the emissions figure for surrender is not yet recorded or the operator believes the recorded figure may be incorrect.
facts.expected_handling: Do not suspend the legal deadline merely because a registry figure is disputed or pending.

facts.source_fact: The emissions figure for surrender is maritime emissions minus any surrender deduction, with one allowance required for each tonne of CO2 equivalent in that figure.
facts.expected_handling: Keep emissions, deduction and allowance quantity as separate fields.

facts.source_fact: A 50% surrender deduction applies to qualifying voyages between Northern Ireland and Great Britain; all emissions must still be monitored and reported even though only 50% are surrendered for.
facts.expected_handling: Apply deduction only to surrender quantity, not to monitored/reported emissions.

guard_patterns.handling: Separate registry compliance functions from emissions measurement.
Require UK allowance instrument for compliance.
Require issued monitoring plan before account creation assumption.
Apply 2026-27 combined and later annual deadlines correctly.
Do not suspend deadline because figure is pending/disputed.
Keep maritime emissions, deduction and surrender figure separate.
Apply 50% deduction only to qualifying NI-GB surrender quantity.
Registry balances do not create vessel-level measured emissions.
Flag allowance, deadline, deduction or permission conflicts.
